children: Smiths Group's results for fiscal 2026 beat expectations and the U.K. industrial-engineering company issued guidance for the year ahead that was possibly better than the market feared, particularly for its Flex-Tek business, Jefferies analysts say in a research note. "We suspect that the Flex-Tek outlook will be a positive surprise for many, as there are good drivers of growth in the division--data centers, aerospace--, a lack of destocking that impacted last year, positive pricing, and [management] is not assuming a U.S. construction recovery next year," the analysts say. For the group as a whole, Smiths guided for organic revenue growth of about 4% and a headline operating profit margin of around 21% in fiscal 2027, which compare with consensus forecasts of 3.9% and 21%, respectively, according to Jefferies. Shares rise 4.1%. (adria.calatayud@wsj.com)
